lean.faithfulness_note: STATEMENT ONLY overall (one sorry: mgo_qsqrt2, the cited fact that the q-real exists in Z[[q]] and satisfies q^2 y^2 - (q^3-1) y - (q^2+1) = 0; Morier-Genoud--Ovsienko Prop. 4.5 as cited in the evidence). Proved without it, by a direct induction on the mod-2 reduction of the coefficient recurrence (no automaton): every y in Z[[q]] solving the equation has c_n even for n = 1 mod 3 (even_of_equation). c_n is defined as the coefficientwise limit of the q-rational convergents R L^2 (R^2 L^2)^m (even-length words, ratio of first-column entries of the q-deformed product) in Q((q)); uniqueness of the limit is proved. A separate finite-range computation (n<40) is about the recurrence-defined sequence only and is labelled so. The Christol-Walnut argument is not formalised; the Lean proof is a different, shorter argument. Numerical check outside Lean: convergents m=2,4,6 agree with the equation solution through q^9, q^17, q^25 (first differing coefficients at q^10, q^18, q^26). Referee note: the single sorry bundles three things, the convergence of the even-length convergents in Z[[q]], the choice of that convergent sequence, and MGO Proposition 4.5 (equation 17); it is not only Proposition 4.5.
lean.covers: Lean proves that any integer power series solving MGO's equation q^2y^2-(q^3-1)y-(q^2+1)=0 has even coefficients at n = 1 mod 3; that [sqrt2]_q is such a series (convergence plus MGO Proposition 4.5) is cited, not proved in Lean.
